Both plan ids are exactly the ledger PR's dependsOn (['audit-overview','contracts','progress']), matching PUBLICATION.md's rule that 'a PR merges only after its dependsOn PRs are on main, so no markdown link points at an unpublished file at merge time'. The two https:// links are external GitHub PR URLs (#1637, #1638), outside the origin/main blob-existence check per the plan's own PR body note -- not evaluated for liveness (out of scope for a read-only git-based check), but present a plausible and correctly-formed GitHub PR URL pattern; no defect.

Branch-only failure claim (worktree with only this PR's 4 files, missing DELIVERY.md/WORKERS.md/PROGRESS.md, expected ENOENT on DELIVERY.md) was verified by static inspection rather than live re-execution, to avoid creating any file outside the four permitted receipts: read validate-roadmap.mjs's top-of-script read order (roadmap.json -> admission-snapshot.json -> repoRoot-relative inventory.json -> DELIVERY.md, in that order, lines 32-39) and confirmed (a) docs/audits/2026-09-12-customizer-spec-reconciliation/inventory.json exists on origin/main (so the inventory read would succeed on a worktree built from main+this-branch), and (b) DELIVERY.md/WORKERS.md/PROGRESS.md all fail git cat-file -e on both origin/main and this branch's diff (confirmed via git diff --name-only origin/main..branch, which lists only the 4 planned files). Given the read order, the first failure on such a worktree would indeed be DELIVERY.md's fs.readFileSync, consistent with the PR body's quoted 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, open ...DELIVERY.md' message and exit code 1. roadmap.json on the branch: sha256 matches the root checkout file exactly (see item 1). stateNormalization20260915: present as an object with keys {at, reason, rule, changed}; `changed` is an array of exactly 19 entries (R2.receipts, R2.triage, R2.combat, R2.authority, R2.authority-live, R2.camp-0..camp-8, R4.S3, R4.S7, R0.publish, R2.authority-client, R2.authority-cutover). Every one of the 73 roadmap.json nodes has a `state` value in the twelve-value enum read directly from DELIVERY.md's 'Allowed slice states' line (planned, admitted, implementing, local-verified, pr-open, review-required, ci-running, merged, main-verified, archived, complete, blocked) -- 0 nodes with an out-of-enum state, confirmed programmatically.
